atomic_claims.text: For every finite simple graph, cp<=p23=m-2nu=lambda+2(nu_star-nu), with lambda the equality-constrained fractional edge-and-triangle partition.
A separator-induction clique-suffix lemma and signed-neighborhood compression, with explicit rational split certificates, give lambda<=floor(n(n+1)/6) on all chordal graphs.

The source-backed fixed-K3 packing theorem and an isolate-preserving bridge give cp<=B(n)+2a(n), with a(n)=o(n^2) uniformly over n-vertex graphs; a fixed epsilon=eta/4 proves the requested quantifiers.
For integer near-extremizer sequences, every optimal lambda-dual compression is eventually low-core, with r=n/3+o(n), t=2n/3+o(n), theta=n/3+o(n), P=o(n), R+D=o(n^2).
In the dense branch, s=B(n)-lambda gives t<=1+sqrt(6s) and cp<=n(1+sqrt(6s))+1; this supplies the explicit subsequence contradiction.
